summary:
Flame in Freefall is an interactive website developed to turn complex NASA research on fire in microgravity into clear and engaging information. It uses scientific explanations, animated visuals and three learning modes (Explore, Learning and Research) to make the science accessible to different audiences. The website highlights NASA investigations such as FLEX, BASS and SAFFIRE, as well as the Apollo 13 mission, showing how real space research and missions connect to fire safety and spacecraft reliability. We also developed the Flame to Failure simulator, which demonstrates how a fire can develop, the precautions astronauts should take and the possible risks to their crew and spacecraft.

Rather than simply displaying NASA data, our project brings it to life through interactive learning and visual demonstrations. It helps people understand the challenges of fire in space and why knowing how to prevent and respond to these hazards is important for astronaut safety.
details:
Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data

Our project is an interactive website that transforms complex NASA research on fire in microgravity into clear and engaging information. It uses three learning modes (Explore, Learning and Research), animated demonstrations and interactive simulators to explain flame behaviour, NASA experiments such as FLEX, BASS and SAFFIRE, and the importance of astronaut fire safety.

Benefits and Intended Impact:
The website makes scientific information easier to understand, raises awareness of fire hazards in space and connects research to practical astronaut safety.

Tools and Technologies:
We used HTML, CSS and JavaScript to develop the website, NASA research resources for scientific content, and Netlify for online hosting.

Creativity:
Instead of simply displaying NASA data, we bring it to life through animations, interactive questions and the Flame to Failure and astronaut safety simulators.

Factors Considered:
We focused on scientific accuracy, different audience knowledge levels, user-friendly design, accessibility and the importance of crew safety.
